stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Fix a big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$, and let $\mathcal U\simeq\mathcal S_U$ be represented by an algebraic space $U$ over $S$. Given $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$, put $\mathcal R=\mathcal U\times_{f,\mathcal X,f}\mathcal U$, whose objects over each $T/S$ are triples $(a,b,\alpha:f(a)\overset{\sim}\to f(b))$. The diagonal of $\mathcal X$ guarantees that $\mathcal R$ is represented by an algebraic space $R$. Its projections yield source and target $s,t:R\to U$, and composition of isomorphisms defines a groupoid multiplication $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$; the convention for arrows is from $s$ to $t$, and reversing a groupoid gives an equivalent groupoid convention. Denote by $[U/R]$ the associated quotient stack; without an atlas condition this need not be algebraic.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ which
is representable by an algebraic space.
Let $f : \mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ be a 1-morphism. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $2$-fibre product
$\mathcal{R} = \mathcal{U} \times_{f, \mathcal{X}, f} \mathcal{U}$
is representable by an algebraic space,
\item there is a canonical equivalence
$$
\mathcal{U} \times_{f, \mathcal{X}, f} \mathcal{U}
\times_{f, \mathcal{X}, f} \mathcal{U} =
\mathcal{R} \times_{\text{pr}_1, \mathcal{U}, \text{pr}_0} \mathcal{R},
$$
\item the projection $\text{pr}_{02}$ induces via (2) a $1$-morphism
$$
\text{pr}_{02} :
\mathcal{R} \times_{\text{pr}_1, \mathcal{U}, \text{pr}_0} \mathcal{R}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{R}
$$
\item let $U$, $R$ be the algebraic spaces representing
$\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{R}$ and $t, s : R \to U$ and
$c : R \times_{s, U, t} R \to R$ are the morphisms corresponding
to the $1$-morphisms
$\text{pr}_0, \text{pr}_1 : \mathcal{R} \to \mathcal{U}$
and
$\text{pr}_{02} :
\mathcal{R} \times_{\text{pr}_1, \mathcal{U}, \text{pr}_0} \mathcal{R} \to
\mathcal{R}$ above, then the quintuple $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is a groupoid in
algebraic spaces over $S$,
\item the morphism $f$ induces a canonical $1$-morphism
$f_{can} : [U/R] \to \mathcal{X}$
of stacks in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, and
\item the $1$-morphism $f_{can} : [U/R] \to \mathcal{X}$ is fully faithful.
\end{enumerate}

Given $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$, put $\mathcal R=\mathcal U\times_{f,\mathcal X,f}\mathcal U$, whose objects over each $T/S$ are triples $(a,b,\alpha:f(a)\overset{\sim}\to f(b))$. The diagonal of $\mathcal X$ guarantees that $\mathcal R$ is represented by an algebraic space $R$. Its projections yield source and target $s,t:R\to U$, and composition of isomorphisms defines a groupoid multiplication $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$; the convention for arrows is from $s$ to $t$, and reversing a groupoid gives an equivalent groupoid convention. Denote by $[U/R]$ the associated quotient stack; without an atlas condition this need not be algebraic.
Let $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ be a 1-morphism from a category fibred in groupoids represented by an algebraic space, to an algebraic stack.
conclusions: $\mathcal R=\mathcal U\times_\mathcal X\mathcal U$ is represented by an algebraic space.
The triple 2-fibre product is equivalent to $\mathcal R\times_\mathcal U\mathcal R$.
Projection to first and last factors defines the composition map.
The induced algebraic-space data $(U,R,s,t,c)$ form a groupoid.

reason: Although all six parts are addressed, part (4) lists pr_0 twice for the groupoid source/target maps, and part (5) appears to reverse the displayed direction of an inverse composite. These are concrete convention/direction ambiguities requiring review rather than a clean plausibility finding.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
Let $U$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : \mathcal{S}_U \to \mathcal{X}$ be a surjective smooth morphism.
Let $(U,R,s,t,c)$ be the arrow groupoid formed from the 2-fibre product $\mathcal S_U\times_\mathcal X\mathcal S_U$, and $f_{can}:[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ the canonical fully faithful 1-morphism it induces.
\begin{enumerate}
\item the morphisms $s$, $t$ are smooth, and
\item the $1$-morphism $f_{can} : [U/R] \to \mathcal{X}$
is an equivalence.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack and $f:\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ a smooth surjective 1-morphism from the stack represented by an algebraic space $U$.
conclusions: The source and target $s,t:R\to U$ are smooth.
The canonical $f_{can}:[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ is an equivalence.

reason: Transfers smoothness of the groupoid structure maps and proves essential surjectivity of the canonical quotient-stack map using local lifts and effective descent.
